title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, retrospective and roadmap
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates the Platform team’s canonical inventory of systems and services, standard how-tos for common operational tasks, dashboard and alerting conventions, prioritized runbooks for frequently-observed incidents, a short retrospective on Q1–Q2 2026 operational work, and the near-term roadmap for platform reliability and observability. It is intended for platform engineers, SRE, and on-call responders.

Scope:
- Services covered: control-plane-api, serving-runtime, request-router, kv-cache, batching-service, metrics-collector, tracing-proxy, autoscaler, and internal tooling (deploy-runner, canary-operator).
- Environments: prod (us-east-1), prod-eu (eu-west-1), stage, and private customer clusters (VPC-onprem).

Systems & services inventory (short):
- control-plane-api — owner: platform-api; SLO: 99.95% 1min availability; tags: api, control-plane.
- serving-runtime — owner: serving-runtime; SLO: 99.9% uptime for scheduled GPU capacity; latency p50 < 80ms for short requests.
- request-router — owner: routing; routes by region/tier/model-variant.
- kv-cache — owner: caching; TTLs: default 30m; eviction policy: LRU with warmup prefetch for hot prefixes.
- batching-service — owner: batching; responsible for request grouping and cost-aware shaping.
- autoscaler — owner: infra-autoscale; scales serving pools based on token-rate and pending queue length.

How-tos (operational patterns):
1) Add a dashboard panel to the Platform Overview dashboard:
   - Navigate to Grafana > Dashboards > Platform > Platform Overview.
   - Create a new panel, select data source: metrics-collector.prometheus.
   - Example PromQL for average serving latency (50ms bucket):
     avg_over_time(serving_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.05",env="prod"}[5m])
   - Set thresholds: warning=150ms, critical=300ms; annotate with runbook link.
   - Save with tag: platform-overview.

2) Create a new alert rule (example):
   - Rule name: ServingRuntime_High_Latency_5m.
   - PromQL (simplified):
     increase(serving_runtime_request_count[5m]) > 0 and (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(serving_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.3)
   - Severity labels: severity=critical, team=serving-runtime.
   - PagerDuty:Platform-Primary (PD escalation policy).
   - Runbook link: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbooks-dashboards-alerts-roadmap-2026-q2-retrospective.json#runbooks

Dashboards & alerting conventions:
- Dashboard naming: team-area / purpose — e.g., Platform / Serving Runtime / Pool Health.
- Panel style guide: p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, request-rate, GPU-utilization, queue-length, cache-hit-rate.
- Alert severities and expected response SLA:
  - P0 (critical): page immediately (PD), ack within 5m, remediate or escalate within 30m.
  - P1 (high): page (PD) or notify slack #platform-oncall, ack within 15m.
  - P2 (medium): slack notification only, action within next business day.
- Escalation routing: alerts must include team and PD service. Use label team=<owner-team>. If owner missing, route to platform-oncall.

Runbooks (canonical procedures):
- Incident: Serving runtime high tail latency (p95/p99)
  1. Triage: Check Grafana Platform > Serving Runtime > Latency (5m/15m). Confirm p95/p99 elevated across pools or isolated to pool.
  2. Check batching-service and kv-cache metrics: batch_size, pending_queue_length, cache_hit_rate.
  3. If pending_queue_length > 1000 or batch_size drop < configured_min (default 4):
     a. Inspect autoscaler scaling activity: kubectl -n serving get hpa,pods,deploy -l pool=<pool-name>.
     b. If nodes saturated (GPU util > 92%), trigger manual scale with autoscaler override: kubectl annotate pool/<pool> platform.autoscale/override=manual --overwrite; scale to desired replicas based on 95th percentile token-rate.
  4. Investigate model fallback events: check request-router logs for fallbacks -> route to smaller variant if necessary.
  5. Mitigation: enable degraded-mode config (route small requests to low-latency variant) via: curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/policy/route-adjust -d '{"pool":"<pool>","variant":"low-latency"}' 
  6. Post-incident: capture timeline, alerts, impacted customers, and open a retrospective ticket (label: incident/serving-latency)

- Incident: GPU OOM in serving-runtime pod
  1. Identify the pod: kubectl -n serving get pods --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide | grep OOM
  2. Inspect pod events and logs: kubectl describe pod <pod> ; kubectl logs <pod> -c model-runner --previous
  3. If reproducible by model variant & sequence length, gate the variant: update model-variant annotation model.gating/disabled=true via control-plane API.
  4. If whole pool impacted, drain pod(s) and restart with reduced max_sequence_length (config map override):
     kubectl set env ds/serving-runtime MAX_SEQ=1024 -n serving --overwrite
  5. Notify model-onboarding and SRE to triage quantization/profile mismatch.

- Incident: Metrics/alerting pipeline lag or missing data
  1. Check metrics-collector health: systemctl status metrics-collector (on VM) or kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=metrics-collector.
  2. Validate Prometheus remote_write connectivity and retention.
  3. If Prometheus is overloaded, apply retention temp increase: /ops/prometheus/adjust-retention.sh --hours 72

Runbook checklist for post-incident review:
- Timeline & root cause hypothesis.
- Evidence (logs, traces, dashboard screenshots).
- Customer impact and rollback steps executed.
- Action items with owners and due dates.
- Link to follow-up ticket in Jira (project: PLAT-OPS).

Retrospective (Q1–Q2 2026 highlights):
- Summary: We had two P0 serving-latency incidents (2026-03-12, 2026-05-04) driven by a combination of increased short-request traffic (burst from a PLG customer experiment) and an upstream change in batching policy that reduced effective batch sizes for certain routes.
- What worked: autoscaler override and low-latency variant fallback limited customer-facing errors to <5% of requests; runbooks enabled quick triage.
- What failed: alerts were noisy (high false positives) due to a single Prometheus rule missing a label filter; dashboards lacked a clear panel for per-customer latency which slowed impact analysis.
- Action items (owner — due):
  - Add per-customer latency panels to Platform Overview (Maya Chen — 2026-06-24).
  - Fix Prometheus alert rule label filters and add unit tests for alert-silence (Diego Martinez — 2026-06-15).
  - Update batching policy rollout checklist to include canary traffic test (Priya Singh — 2026-06-30).

Roadmap & next steps (next 3 months):
- Observability: ship per-customer latency dashboards and a synthetic workload runner to generate repeatable traffic for canaries (owner: observability; ETA: 2026-07-15).
- Alerts: migrate alerting rules to alertmanager v1.6 with schema validation and add automated dry-run for new alerts (owner: platform-sre; ETA: 2026-07-01).
- Runtime: add adaptive batching experiment for small request patterns (owner: serving-runtime; ETA: 2026-08-01).
- Private deployments: publish a hardened alerting baseline and sample Grafana dashboards for customer-managed Prometheus (owner: eng-private-deployments; ETA: 2026-08-15).

Appendix: sample alert rule (YAML example, annotated)

# Sample PrometheusRule: ServingRuntime_High_Latency_5m
# apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
# kind: PrometheusRule
# metadata:
#   name: servingruntime-high-latency
#   namespace: monitoring
# spec:
#   groups:
#   - name: serving-runtime.rules
#     rules:
#     - alert: ServingRuntimeHighLatency5m
#       expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(serving_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.3
#       labels:
#         severity: critical
#         team: serving-runtime
#       annotations:
#         summary: "Serving runtime p95 latency > 300ms (5m)"
